The World Bank-commissioned assessment of Libya's primary care system, carried out in January to May 2021 and citing WHO's Libya Annual Report 2020, states that medical records are still paper-based, that there is no national electronic health records system and that existing records systems are not interoperable.

The same assessment, done in 2021 and citing WHO's Libya Annual Report 2020, states that health management systems are not in routine use at the national or local level, and that DHIS-2 was then being implemented and at a piloting stage.

The assessment, done in 2021, states that epidemiological data are recorded by a national Health Information System that collates facility-level data from paper records, and that health intelligence is not routinely gathered or used at the facility level; it does not say where or whether the collated data is keyed.

WHO's Libya annual report for 2023 states that WHO continued to advance the health information system work plan during 2023, with efforts to expand and integrate systems such as DHIS2 and its Health Information Management Unit giving technical support towards a unified HIS with systematic data reporting.

The Ministry of Health's own page states that its Health Information and Documentation Centre, set up within the Ministry in 2006, introduced DHIS2 as the electronic system for routine data collection from health facilities and runs it as the central platform for routine statistics and health surveys; the page is undated and its newest content is from 2022, used here as the date.
